Content: **Proto-Indo-Iranian \*mitrás** ‘covenant; treaty; agreement; promise’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *miθráh, Proto-Indo-Aryan *mitrás, Avestan 𐬨𐬌𐬚𐬭𐬀. Reconstruction credited to Turner, CDIAL.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Áryas** ‘autonymic (self-identifying) ethnonym of the respective Indo-Iranian peoples, i.e. the Indo-Aryans and the Iranians.’. No accepted Proto-Indo-European etymology; the article marks the origin as unknown or disputed. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Áryah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Áryas. Reconstruction credited to Mallory–Adams, EIEC; Mallory–Adams, Oxford Introduction.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*wíćš** ‘village; household’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *wícš, Proto-Indo-Aryan *wíṭṣ, Old Avestan 𐬬𐬍𐬯, Old Persian 𐎻𐎰. Reconstruction credited to Mallory–Adams, Oxford Introduction; Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*ćatám** ‘hundred’. From Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *catám, Proto-Indo-Aryan *śatám, Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬀, Old Persian *θatam. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*mánas** ‘mind, intellect, thought’. From Proto-Indo-European *ménos. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *mánah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *mánas, Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬀𐬵, Old Persian 𐎶𐎴𐏃.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hámsas** ‘shoulder’. From Proto-Indo-European *h₃émsos. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hámhah.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hnā́ma** ‘name’. From Proto-Indo-European *h₁nómn̥. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hnā́ma, Proto-Nuristani *nāma, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hnā́ma.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*káHmas** ‘wish, desire’. From Proto-Indo-European *kóh₂mos. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *káHmah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *káHmas. Reconstruction credited to Rix, LIV².

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*bʰr̥ȷ́ʰáns** ‘high, tall’. From Proto-Indo-European *bʰérǵʰonts. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *br̥jáns.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*dáća** ‘ten’. From Proto-Indo-European *déḱm̥. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *dáca, Proto-Nuristani *daca, Proto-Indo-Aryan *dáśa.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*gʰawš-** ‘to hear’. No accepted Proto-Indo-European etymology; the article marks the origin as unknown or disputed. Witnesses: Proto-Indo-Aryan *gʰawṣ-. Reconstruction credited to Rix, LIV²; Cheung, EDIV.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*gā́wš** ‘cow’. From Proto-Indo-European *gʷṓws. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *gā́wš, Proto-Indo-Aryan *gā́wṣ. Reconstruction credited to Rastorgueva–Edel'man, ESIJa.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*-H**. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *-H, Proto-Indo-Aryan *-H. Reconstruction credited to Martínez García–de Vaan, Introduction to Avestan.

Reconstruction credited to Mayrhofer, EWAia; Wodtko–Irslinger–Schneider, NIL; Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon; Mallory–Adams, EIEC.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*dʰáHyas** ‘nourishing, sustaining; helping, supporting’. From Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁(y)-. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *gáwdaHyah, Avestan *dāiiā̊, Old Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬊𐬛𐬁𐬌𐬌𐬋.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*dʰáyȷ́ʰas**. From Proto-Indo-European *dʰóyǵʰos. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *dáyjah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *dáyźʰas, Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬉𐬰𐬀.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*pHtás** ‘drunk’. From Proto-Indo-European *ph₃tós.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*ȷ́ʰžʰā́s** ‘the ground, earth’. From Proto-Indo-European *dʰéǵʰōm. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *jā́h.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*ȷ́ʰā́rd** ‘heart’. From Proto-Indo-European *ḱḗr. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *jā́rd. Reconstruction credited to Kümmel 2015.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*-wants**. From Proto-Indo-European *-wénts. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *-wāh, Avestan -𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬥. Reconstruction credited to Lipp, Die Palatale im Indoiranischen; Martínez García–de Vaan, Introduction to Avestan.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*raHíš** ‘wealth, property, goods’. From Proto-Indo-European *reh₁ís. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *raHíš, Proto-Indo-Aryan *raHíṣ, Avestan 𐬭𐬀𐬉𐬬𐬀𐬥𐬙.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Háȷ́ʰr̥** ‘day’. From Proto-Indo-European *dʰeǵʰ-. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Háyr̥, Old Avestan 𐬀𐬌𐬌𐬁𐬭𐬇, Young Avestan 𐬀𐬌𐬌𐬀𐬭𐬆. Reconstruction credited to Kümmel 2015; Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon; Mayrhofer, EWAia.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*HubʰáH** ‘both’. From Proto-Indo-European *bʰóh₁. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hubáyah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hubʰáyas, Old Avestan 𐬎𐬠𐬀, Young Avestan 𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬌𐬌𐬀, Old Persian 𐎢𐎲𐎠. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon; Dunkel, LIPP.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hānušákš** ‘in due course, one after the other, one by one’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hānušaxš, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hānuṣákṣ, Avestan 𐬁𐬥𐬎𐬱𐬵𐬀𐬑𐬱. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hwr̥ȷ́ánam** ‘encampment, community, village, settlement’. From Proto-Indo-European *h₁wreǵ-. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hwr̥janyas, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hwr̥janyas, Avestan 𐬬𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬰𐬇𐬥𐬌𐬌𐬀, Old Avestan 𐬬𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬰𐬇𐬥𐬀, Young Avestan 𐬬𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬰𐬁𐬥𐬀, Old Persian 𐎺𐎼𐎭𐎴𐎶.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*gasćáti** ‘to step, go’. From Proto-Indo-European *gʷm̥sḱéti. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *gascati, Avestan 𐬘𐬀𐬯𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌. Reconstruction credited to Lipp, Die Palatale im Indoiranischen; Rastorgueva–Edel'man, ESIJa.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*wáHr̥** ‘water’. From Proto-Indo-European *wódr̥. Witnesses: Avestan 𐬬𐬁𐬭.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*wárčas** ‘vital power, energy; light, lustre, splendour, brilliance’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *wárčahwants, Proto-Indo-Aryan *wárćaswants, Avestan 𐬬𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬗𐬀𐬤𐬵𐬀𐬧𐬙.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hyaštā́** ‘worshipper, one who worships’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hyaštā́, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hyaṣṭā́, Avestan 𐬫𐬀𐬱𐬙𐬀𐬭. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Háynas** ‘sin, crime, offense’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Háynah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Háynas, Avestan 𐬀𐬉𐬥𐬀𐬵. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, The Indo-Iranian substratum.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*krináHti** ‘to buy, purchase’. From Proto-Indo-European *kʷrinéh₂ti. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *xrináHti, Proto-Indo-Aryan *krináHti. Reconstruction credited to Cheung, EDIV.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*pʰáynas** ‘foam, froth; saliva, mucus’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *fáynah. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky 1988; Mayrhofer, EWAia; Rastorgueva–Edel'man, ESIJa; Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*mána**. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *mána, Old Avestan 𐬨𐬇⸱𐬥𐬁, Young Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬀, Old Persian 𐎶𐎴𐎠. Reconstruction credited to Dunkel, LIPP; Mayrhofer, EWAia; Rastorgueva–Edel'man, ESIJa.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*-ám**. From Proto-Indo-European *-óm. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *-ám, Proto-Indo-Aryan *-ám.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*tuHám**. From Proto-Indo-European *túh₂. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *tuHám, Proto-Indo-Aryan *tuHám, Old Avestan 𐬙𐬎𐬎𐬇𐬨, Young Avestan 𐬙𐬏𐬨, Old Persian 𐎬𐎺𐎶. Reconstruction credited to Dunkel, LIPP; Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*asmá** ‘us’. From Proto-Indo-European *n̥smé. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *ahmá, Proto-Indo-Aryan *asmā́m, Old Avestan 𐬇𐬵𐬨𐬁, Young Avestan 𐬀𐬵𐬨𐬀. Reconstruction credited to Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL; Dunkel, LIPP.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*táwa**. From Proto-Indo-European *téwe. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *táwa, Proto-Indo-Aryan *táwa, Old Avestan 𐬙𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬁, Young Avestan 𐬙𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬀. Reconstruction credited to Dunkel, LIPP; Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL; Mayrhofer, EWAia; Abaev, Osetinskij slovar'.

Content: **Proto-Indo-Iranian \*máȷ́ʰyas** ‘bigger, greater’. From Proto-Indo-European *méǵyōs. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *májyah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *máźʰyas, Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬰𐬌𐬌𐬀𐬵.

Content: **Proto-Indo-Iranian \*stabdʰás** ‘hard, firm’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *stabdáh, Old Persian *staftah.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hr̥HwáraH** ‘fertile land’. Witnesses: Avestan 𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬭𐬁. Reconstruction credited to Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL; Kümmel 2017.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*payćás** ‘adorned, decorated’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *wicwápaycah, Avestan 𐬬𐬍𐬯𐬞𐬋𐬞𐬀𐬉𐬯𐬀𐬵. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon; de Vaan, The Avestan Vowels.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*tawHás** ‘strong, mighty’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *táwHyah, Old Persian 𐎫𐎢𐎻𐎡𐎹𐎠. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*táwHas** ‘strength, might’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *táwHah, Avestan *tawah, Young Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌⸱𐬙𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬃. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*pŕ̥ts** ‘fight, struggle, battle’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *parwans, Young Avestan 𐬞𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬥𐬈, Old Persian *nipr̥tah. Reconstruction credited to Bailey, Dictionary of Khotan Saka; Cheung, EDIV; Rix, LIV².

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*(H)yaȷ́ʰúš** ‘young, youthful’. No accepted Proto-Indo-European etymology; the article marks the origin as unknown or disputed. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *(H)yajúš, Old Avestan 𐬫𐬀𐬰𐬎. Reconstruction credited to Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL; Lubotsky, The Indo-Iranian substratum.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hr̥Htás** ‘ground’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hr̥Htáh, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hr̥Htás.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*čyáwatay** ‘to move, go’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *šyáwatay, Proto-Indo-Aryan *ćyáwatay, Old Avestan 𐬳𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬉, Old Persian 𐎠𐏁𐎡𐎹𐎺<ts:ašiyava>. Reconstruction credited to Rix, LIV²; Cheung, EDIV.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*ǰʰantā́** ‘one who strikes or hits; one who kills, a killer’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *ǰantā́, Proto-Nuristani *janta, Proto-Indo-Aryan *źʰantā́, Avestan 𐬘𐬀𐬧𐬙𐬀𐬭, Old Persian 𐎩𐎫𐎼.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*pištás** ‘crushed, ground; flour, meal; anything ground or crushed’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *pištáh. Reconstruction credited to Cantera 2017.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*spáćyati** ‘to see’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *spácyati, Proto-Indo-Aryan *spáśyati, Old Avestan 𐬯𐬞𐬀𐬯𐬌𐬌𐬁, Young Avestan 𐬯𐬞𐬀𐬯𐬌𐬌𐬈𐬌𐬙𐬌.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hastā́** ‘one who shoots; an archer, marksman, a bowman’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hastā́, Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hastā́, Avestan 𐬀𐬯𐬙𐬀𐬭.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*ćaHstā́** ‘one who commands, directs, rules’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *pracaHstā́, Proto-Indo-Aryan *praśaHstā́, Avestan 𐬟𐬭𐬀𐬯𐬁𐬯𐬙𐬀𐬭.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*bʰráHtr̥wyas** ‘brother's son, nephew; fraternal relation, a paternal cousin’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *bráHtr̥wyas, Proto-Indo-Aryan *bʰráHtr̥wyas, Avestan 𐬠𐬭𐬁𐬙𐬭𐬎𐬌𐬌𐬀.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*tápati** ‘to be hot’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *tápati, Proto-Indo-Aryan *tápati. Reconstruction credited to Cheung, EDIV.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*taptás** ‘warmed, heated, hot’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *taftáh, Proto-Indo-Aryan *taptás, Avestan 𐬙𐬀𐬟𐬙𐬀. Reconstruction credited to Abaev, Osetinskij slovar'.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*ȷ́ʰwar-** ‘to go crookedly’. Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwer-. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *jwárati, Proto-Indo-Aryan *źʰwárati, Young Avestan 𐬰𐬠𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬨𐬥𐬀. Reconstruction credited to Cheung, EDIV; Rix, LIV².
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*traHtā́** ‘protector, savior’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *θraHtā́, Proto-Indo-Aryan *traHtā́, Avestan 𐬚𐬭𐬁𐬙𐬀𐬭.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*HawasáHanam** ‘act of unharnessing horses; a place of halting and rest; end, completion, conclusion’. From Proto-Indo-European *seh₂-. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *HawaháHanam, Proto-Indo-Aryan *HawasáHanam, Avestan 𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬢𐬵𐬁𐬥𐬀.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*HabʰidʰáHanam** ‘a halter or a bridle’. From Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *HabidáHanam, Proto-Indo-Aryan *HabʰidʰáHaniH, Avestan 𐬀𐬌𐬡𐬌𐬜𐬁𐬥𐬀.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*mastr̥ǰʰā́** ‘brain’. No accepted Proto-Indo-European etymology; the article marks the origin as unknown or disputed. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *mastr̥gā́, Young Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬯𐬙𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬖𐬥𐬀𐬯𐬗𐬀.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*sarwátaHts** ‘wholeness’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *harwátaHth, Proto-Indo-Aryan *sarwátaHts, Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬙𐬁𐬝, Old Persian *𐏃𐎢𐎽𐎺𐎫𐎠𐎫. Reconstruction credited to Martínez García–de Vaan, Introduction to Avestan.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*wadʰúHs** ‘bride; young wife’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *wadúHs. Reconstruction credited to Klein–Joseph–Fritz, HCHIEL; Mayrhofer, EWAia; Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon.

Content: **Proto-Indo-Iranian \*Hŕ̥ȷ́atam** ‘silver’. From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *Hŕ̥jatam. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon; Rastorgueva–Edel'man, ESIJa.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*turíHyas** ‘fourth’. Witnesses: Avestan 𐬙𐬏𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬀. Reconstruction credited to Martínez García–de Vaan, Introduction to Avestan.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*dʰaHnáH** ‘seed, grain’. From Proto-Indo-European *dʰoHnéh₂. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *daHnáH, Proto-Indo-Aryan *dʰaHnáH, Avestan 𐬛𐬁𐬥𐬁. Reconstruction credited to Kümmel 2017; Turner, CDIAL.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*HyánHtā** ‘husband's brother's wife’. From Proto-Indo-European [[*h₁yénh₂tēr. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *HyánHtā. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon; Rastorgueva–Edel'man, ESIJa.

Content: **Proto-Indo-Iranian \*winátˢti** ‘to find, seek; to obtain, recieve’. From Proto-Indo-European [[*winédti. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *winásti. Reconstruction credited to Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon.
**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*čánHas** ‘desire’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *čínHah, Proto-Indo-Aryan *ćánHas, Avestan -𐬗𐬌𐬥𐬀𐬵-, Old Persian *canah. Reconstruction credited to Rix, LIV²; Cheung, EDIV.

**Proto-Indo-Iranian \*čakánHa** ‘to be pleased, delighted’. Witnesses: Proto-Iranian *čakánHa, Old Avestan 𐬗𐬁𐬑𐬥𐬀𐬭𐬆, Young Avestan 𐬗𐬀𐬐𐬀𐬥𐬀. Reconstruction credited to Rix, LIV²; Lubotsky, Indo-Aryan Inherited Lexicon; Mayrhofer, EWAia; Rastorgueva–Edel'man, ESIJa; Cheung, EDIV.
